N1.s: Du har brugt dine %lld gratis Cutlings. Fortsæt i Cutling og lås op, så bliver den nye gemt.
N1.back: You have used your 5 free Cutlings. Continue in Cutling and lock up, then becomes the new-one saved.
N1.why: Opens with S3's words so the limit is said the same way everywhere. Siri may read it aloud with nothing on screen, so "den nye" names the item being added. No comma between two imperatives joined by og; the ", så" result clause follows S28. 89 characters.

N2.s: Du har brugt dine %lld gratis Cutlings. Åbn Cutling og lås op, så kan du gemme flere.
N2.back: You have used your 5 free Cutlings. Open Cutling and lock up, then can you save more.
N2.why: N1's shape with Åbn instead of Fortsæt, because here the person has to open the app themselves. "Så kan du gemme flere" echoes S28's "så kan du gemme". "Lås op for at gemme" is avoided: "låse op for" reads as unlocking something else, the problem S14's note gives. 82 characters.

N3.why: A participle and a short tail, the way a Danish toast says it. "Plads" picks up S6's "Plads til". Én takes the accent for the numeral, as in S10. No full stop at the end, as in K1. 29 characters.

N4.why: Same opening as N3, then the count pair from S21 and S29, so 5 af 5 shows the free places are full without saying it twice. Danish puts used before total, so plain %lld works twice. 28 characters.

N5.s: %lld af %lld gratis er brugt. Lås op og gem
N5.back: 5 of 5 free are used. Lock up and save
N5.why: Opens with N4's count so the two capsules match. "Lås op og gem" names what a tap does in two verbs, and gem with no object means the item being saved. "Den" was cut to stay under 40: 37 characters.

N6.why: The bare verb from "Lås Cutling op". The app's name sits in the notice above it, so the button leaves it out. 6 characters.

N7.s: Du har brugt dine %lld gratis Cutlings. Lås Cutling op, så bliver den her gemt.
N7.back: You have used your 5 free Cutlings. Lock Cutling up, then becomes this-one-here saved.
N7.why: Uses S3's opening and the S15 verb. "Den her" points at the item shown in the form; a bare "den" could be read as Cutling, the app. 76 characters.

N8.s: Den her er lagt til side. Åbn Cutling og lås op, så bliver den gemt.
N8.back: This-one-here is laid to side. Open Cutling and lock up, then becomes it saved.
N8.why: "Lagt til side" means kept for later; "gemt" is already the app's word for saved, so it can't mean kept here. The first sentence makes the item the subject, so "den" in the second can only mean the item. 68 characters.
